report.answer: In compose.ts's dispatch(i), each middleware call is individually try/caught: `await handler(context, () => dispatch(i+1))`. Because next() (dispatch(i+1)) executes inside that awaited call, an error surfaces at the innermost active dispatch frame first — if `onError` was supplied to compose() and the thrown value is an Error, it's converted to a Response there and dispatch returns normally (so outer middleware's own try/catch around next() never sees it, only context.error/context.res); otherwise it's rethrown and bubbles to whatever caller does have an onError (or none, in which case it keeps propagating). Hono's #dispatch() supplies `this.errorHandler` (default: unwrap HTTPException via getResponse(), else log + 500; overridable via app.onError()) as compose's onError for the main route stack, and wraps the whole composed(c) call plus the single-handler fast path in its own try/catch as a final safety net for non-Error throws and the "context not finalized" check.

verified.summary: compose()'s dispatch(i) wraps `await handler(context, () => dispatch(i+1))` in try/catch; if `err instanceof Error && onError`, it calls onError(err, context), sets context.error, isError=true, and returns context normally (no rethrow) — swallowing the error before it reaches outer middleware's own try/catch around next().
verified.evidence: src/compose.ts full source (read in turn 1, quoted above)

verified.summary: If onError is absent or the thrown value isn't an Error instance, compose's dispatch rethrows (`else { throw err }`), letting the error propagate to whichever caller/compose call does have error handling.

Hono#dispatch() (src/hono-base.ts line 451) calls `compose(matchResult[0], this.errorHandler, this.#notFoundHandler)`; the default errorHandler (lines 36-43) checks for `'getResponse' in err` (HTTPException-style) and otherwise logs + returns a generic 500, and can be replaced via app.onError() (line 272) which just reassigns `this.errorHandler`.
verified.evidence: /tmp/hono-base.txt lines 36-43, 272-273, 451 (read in this turn and turn 1)

verified.summary: #dispatch wraps `composed(c)` in its own try/catch calling `this.#handleError(err, c)` as a final safety net (for the 'Context is not finalized' throw and any non-Error rethrows), and the single-handler fast path (matchResult[0].length===1, bypassing compose entirely) has its own equivalent try/catch and `.catch()` on the returned promise.

The `every()` combinator in src/middleware/combine/index.ts calls compose() with no onError argument at all, so genuine thrown errors from its sub-middleware are NOT swallowed there — they rethrow out of `every` and are caught by the enclosing app-level compose's dispatch (which does have this.errorHandler); every() also synthesizes a thrown Error('Unmet condition') when a middleware returns `false`.

Mounting sub-apps (hono-base.ts line 226) wraps the mounted app's handler call as `compose([], app.errorHandler)(c, () => r.handler(c, next))`, using compose purely as a try/catch adapter so the sub-app's own errorHandler processes errors from its mounted fetch handler.
